intermediateFindings: The initial Linux native build passed and is retained. Adding custom-directory safety guards and Windows flag quoting required a refreshed recipe; its three archives are byte-identical to the initial archives.
Helper regressions exposed plus-sign filename rejection and case-sensitive notice lookup. Corrected validators preserve path safety and require complete matching runtime reviews.
One external runtime-inspection wrapper lowercased output but retained an uppercase regex; corrected the parser and reused the successful immutable objdump output.
One new test was initially inserted in the wrong scope; moved assertions and reran the focused tests. All earlier helper logs remain retained.

Windows CTest reported all four named tests passed with exit zero using newer summary wording. The external wrapper rejected that wording. Preserved its original failed assessment and driver, validated both summary formats and four rejection cases, and reassessed unchanged raw output without rerunning tests.
Windows policy prevented executing the read-only process query as a script file. The same query ran inline with no policy change and found no owned processes.

timingReview.conclusion: Saved aggregate metrics do not locate the delay in queueing, persistence, transport or host scheduling. No evidence-backed production repair or host-load attribution; no retry until green.

windowsBuildEnvironment: MSYS2 MINGW64; MinGW64 bin before MSYS paths; pinned Rust executables supplied explicitly; no standalone Rust bin prepended to Windows PATH.
